findings.fix: Collect the house number and street together in one address-line field.
findings.violation: The house number has its own field separate from the street, and it is required, so an address with no number cannot be entered.

findings.fix: Replace it with the standard token for this field, for example email.
findings.violation: The autocomplete value e-mail is not a valid autofill detail in the HTML standard, so autofill is broken for this field.

findings.evidence: <label id="acctnum-label" for="acctnum-input">Account number</label> <input id="acctnum-input" name="account_number" type="text" inputmode="numeric" required="">
findings.fix: Remove this field, or make it optional and state what it is for.
findings.violation: Like the membership-number field, this asks for an account number before the account exists, which a person creating a new account cannot supply.

findings.evidence: <label id="member-label" for="member-input">Membership number (8 digits)</label> <input id="member-input" name="membership_number" type="text" inputmode="numeric" placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required="">
findings.fix: Remove this field from account creation, or make it optional for a person linking an existing membership.
findings.violation: A person creating a new account has no membership number yet, so a required field asking for one blocks every first-time signup from completing the form.

findings.evidence: <label id="org-label" for="org-input">Organization name</label> <input id="org-input" name="organization" type="text" style="font-size:16px" required="">
findings.fix: Remove this field, or make it optional and ask for it only for a business account.
findings.violation: Nothing in the form explains why an organization name is required to create this account; most people opening a personal shopping account have none to give.

findings.evidence: <label id="website-label" for="website-input">Company website</label> <input id="website-input" name="website" type="url" required="">
findings.fix: Remove this field, or make it optional and ask for it only when the person indicates a business account.
findings.violation: Creating this account does not use a company website for anything the markup shows, and requiring it blocks every individual signing up who has no company website to give.

findings.evidence: <button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button>, placed between the row-contacttime and row-hear fields
findings.fix: Move the View details control out of the field sequence, placing it beside Submit at the end of the form, or remove it from this form.
findings.violation: This action sits between the Preferred contact time and How did you hear about us fields, interrupting the column of fields, rather than beside the other action at the point where the fields end.

findings.fix: Label the button with the action it performs, such as Create account or Send message.
findings.violation: The form's primary button is labelled Submit, a generic word that says nothing about what pressing it does.
On this name field, autocorrection and spellchecking stay on, so a phone keyboard can change a value it does not know.

findings.fix: Remove the confirmation field and offer a control that shows the password as typed.
findings.violation: The form asks for the new password a second time to confirm it, doubling the typing for every person.

findings.evidence: <label id="contacttime-label" for="contacttime-input" style="display:block">Preferred contact time</label> <input id="contacttime-input" name="contact_time" type="text" required="">
findings.fix: Make this field optional and move it to the account's contact-preferences settings, or remove it.
findings.violation: Creating this account does not need a preferred contact time, and requiring an answer in a free-text field with no stated format forces a decision the task does not use.
